rounds.text: Ausom Enterprise Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation, highlighted by a modest P/E ratio of 8.01x and a price-to-book ratio of 1.25x [E1, E2]. This represents a significant discount compared to sector benchmarks, where the average P/E sits at 26.66x and the EV/EBITDA stands at 14.38x [E6, E11]. Operational efficiency is robust, evidenced by a return on capital employed (ROCE) of 15.07% to 16.2% that comfortably outperforms the sector median of 9.77% [E10, E12]. Top-line expansion has been explosive, driven by a three-year compounded sales growth rate of 127% and a trailing twelve-month surge of 120% [E15, E16]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests substantial intrinsic upside, leaving a margin of safety of 49.6% while the reverse DCF implies that the current price assumes an unduly pessimistic negative earnings growth rate [E43, E45]. The company maintains a healthy financial position with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x and comfortable short-term liquidity supported by a current ratio of 3.03x [E36, E37]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the stock a strong score of 88 out of 100 alongside strong relative-strength ratings and a supportive consumer durables sector tailwind [E49, E60, E65]. Conceded: [E19], [E32], [E34], [E51], [E52], [E59].

The most alarming evidence against Ausom Enterprise Ltd is its severe cash flow deterioration, highlighted by negative operating cash flow of Rs -3 Cr and a staggering free cash flow burn of Rs -24 Cr in March 2026, leading to a dismal cash conversion of -0.16x [E32, E33, E34]. This fundamental disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation is compounded by a declining trailing twelve-month profit growth of -11% and compressed quarterly operating margins falling by two percentage points to 1% in June 2026 compared to the prior year [E19, E29]. Furthermore, earnings quality is heavily distorted because reported profits include non-operating other income of Rs 12.0 Cr, masking underlying operational weakness [E59]. Compounding these operational risks, historical volatility is extreme at 79.4%, paired with a catastrophic historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -96.6% [E51, E52]. Expectations are running dangerously ahead of actual business delivery, as evidenced by price growth exceeding profit growth by 53% recently, while foreign institutional ownership has dwindled down to a negligible 0.13% [E41, E55]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x and a strong 5-year compounded sales growth rate of 35% [E14, E36].

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -3 Cr and free cash flow was Rs -24 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34], and foreign institutional holding stands at 0.13% [E41]. However, the bear's alarm over cash generation ignores that the company maintains robust short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 3.03x and is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.06x [E36, E37]. Conceded: TTM profit growth is -11% and quarterly operating margin fell two percentage points [E19, E29], but this cyclical compression is offset by exceptional multi-year momentum, including a 3-year compounded sales growth of 127% and 3-year profit growth of 152% [E15, E18]. Furthermore, the valuation remains highly compelling despite price gains, trading at a modest P/E of 8.01x and an EV/EBITDA of 5.49x against sector benchmarks of 26.66x and 14.38x [E1, E6, E11]. Finally, the DCF model demonstrates a substantial margin of safety of 49.6% at intrinsic value, with a reverse DCF indicating that the current price only prices in a modest -4.8% earnings growth [E43, E44, E45].

Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x and a current ratio of 3.03x [E36, E37]. However, dismissing the severe cash burn overlooks that operating cash flow plunged to Rs -3 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to Rs -24 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.16x [E32, E33, E34]. Furthermore, while multi-year growth figures look impressive, TTM profit growth has turned negative at -11%, quarterly operating margins have contracted by 2 percentage points year-over-year, and median 5-year ROE sits at a modest 9% [E19, E25, E29]. Conceded: the headline P/E is 8.01x against sector benchmarks [E1, E6], but this cheap multiple is distorted by a material Rs 12.0 Cr block of other income embedded directly within reported earnings [E59]. Finally, relying on theoretical DCF margins of safety ignores the extreme risk profile of a stock carrying a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -96.6% alongside an annualized volatility of 79.4% [E43, E51, E52].

Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to Rs -3 Cr and free cash flow to Rs -24 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34], but this short-term strain is buffered by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x and comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 3.03x [E36, E37]. Conceded: TTM profit growth is -11% [E19] and median 5-year ROE is 9% [E25], yet these figures miss the explosive multi-year trajectory reflected in a 127% compounded sales growth over 3 years and 120% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E16]. Conceded: earnings contain Rs 12.0 Cr of other income [E59], but the core valuation remains exceptionally attractive at a P/E of 8.01x and EV/EBITDA of 5.49x, trading at deep discounts to sector benchmarks of 26.66x and 14.38x respectively [E1, E6, E11]. Finally, historical drawdowns and volatility [E51, E52] are offset by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 292 offering a 49.6% margin of safety alongside a top-tier relative-strength rating of 100 [E43, E44, E49].

Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x and a comfortable current ratio of 3.03x [E36, E37]. However, dismissing the negative operating cash flow of Rs -3 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -24 Cr as short-term strain ignores the reality that operating cash conversion sits at a dismal -0.16x and covers only 32% of operating profit [E32, E34, E35]. While multi-year sales growth figures appear explosive [E15, E16], compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has actually contracted by -11%, the 5-year median return on equity languishes at a low 9%, and recent quarterly operating margins have compressed by 2 percentage points year-over-year [E19, E25, E29]. Conceded: the reported P/E of 8.01x sits below sector benchmarks [E1, E6], but this multiple is artificially flattered by Rs 12.0 Cr of other income embedded within the earnings [E59]. Finally, relying on a model-driven intrinsic value or relative strength [E43, E49] ignores the severe structural risks of an annualized volatility of 79.4% and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -96.6% [E51, E52].
